newsitem.title: UK: Claremont Garments sees slip in H2 profit.
newsitem.headline: Claremont Garments sees slip in H2 profit.

text.p: British clothing maker Claremont Garments (Holdings) Plc, which has reorganised its business this year to improve efficiency, said a combination of some sales weakness and cost overruns meant profits for the second half would be "somewhat below" those of the year-ago period.

Countering this setback, however, the company said that trading for most of the period had been strong and, it added in a statement, it believed that longstanding external pressures on margins in the industry as a whole were starting to ease.
"Prospects for 1997 are good," said the company, whose main customer is large retailing group Marks & Spencer Plc.

"In part this represents our customers' confidence in their own trading outlook, which is now feeding through to the supplier base -- indeed, we are seeing some price increases on existing merchandise," Claremont added.
From a cost point of view, it will take an exceptional charge of 7.0 million stg in this year's accounts to pay for the review that moved all stitching from a factory in Glasgow.
"The necessary actions have now been implemented and we have reduced our cost base, on an on-going basis, by approximately 7.0 million stg per annum," it added.
